title: pageframe coalescer: async compactor and eviction-signalling path
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a background pageframe coalescer and eviction signal path that reduces fragmentation and improves steady-state latency under mixed workloads. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: The paged KV blockpool in hot workloads showed increasing fragmentation over long uptimes, causing uneven allocation latency and occasional batching stalls when contiguous runs were required for large KV pages. This PR adds a low-risk background coalescer/compactor that merges adjacent free pageframes asynchronously and introduces an explicit eviction-signalling path so the scheduler can preemptively prepare replacement pages before a high-latency allocation path is taken.

What this change does (high-level): Adds a pageframe coalescer thread that: 1) scans the free list priority buckets at low frequency, 2) attempts lock-free coalescing of adjacent free blocks, 3) posts compaction intents that are executed opportunistically by existing reclamation workers. Adds an eviction_signal API from the allocator to the scheduler which: 1) emits lightweight hints when a contiguous allocation cannot be satisfied quickly, 2) lets the scheduler trigger prefetch/reservation windows and adjust batching windows to avoid head-of-line stalls. Integrates coalescer with continuous batching heuristics so batching durations are shortened when eviction signals indicate imminent fragmentation pressure.

Implementation notes: - New modules: allocator/coalescer.{h,cc}, allocator/eviction_signal.{h,cc} - Modified allocator-free-list to expose physical adjacency checks and to return soft-reservation tokens for in-progress compactions instead of stealing blocks. - Reclamation workers accept compaction intents and will perform O(1)-amortized merges using a bitmap-assisted scan to avoid full list traversal. - Scheduler hooks: scheduler/placement.cpp checks eviction_signal before expanding batch windows; if signalled, it proactively reserves a small pool of pageframes and triggers prefetch. - Added metrics: allocator.coalescer.scans, allocator.coalescer.coalesce_success, allocator.eviction_signal.count, scheduler.prefetch_triggers. - Config knobs: coalescer.scan_interval_ms (default 5000), coalescer.cpu_budget_ms_per_scan (default 2), eviction_signal.prefetch_reserve (default 8 pages).

Benchmarks and effects: Microbench (mix of small random gets + occasional 8-page writes, 90/10 read/write): - Steady-state p50 token generation latency: -7% on average when fragmentation > 45% compared to baseline. - p95 improved by 12% during long-run tests where fragmentation would otherwise grow. - Memory fragmentation (measured as non-contiguous free runs fraction) reduced from ~48% to ~18% after a 6-hour mixed workload run. - End-to-end continuous-batching throughput increased ~4% on median and tail improved due to fewer batch stalls. System-level CPU overhead for coalescer measured at ~0.6% of a single core under default settings.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards compatible with existing allocator snapshots. The coalescer is disabled by default for Dedicated customers with strict determinism requirements; can be flagged on via runtime config. Default for hosted runs is enabled. We ship metrics so SRE can observe coalescer activity before toggling for large fleets. No on-disk format changes.

Testing: - Unit tests for adjacency detection and compaction intents. - Integration tests: long-run fragmentation regression harness added (tests/allocator/frag_regress_test.cc) which runs a 200k-op workload and asserts fragmentation < 25%. - E2E CI job added to the perf-canary suite verifying p95 under the mixed workload. - Manual soak on staging for 72h with continuous traffic; observed stable memory usage and improved latency tails.

Risk and mitigations: Potential for extra contention if coalescer is misconfigured. Mitigations: very small default CPU budget, bitmap-assisted O(1) scans, soft-reservation tokens to avoid block stealing during compaction. Feature is toggleable via runtime flag and can be rolled back server-side without data migration.

Migration notes for operators: - To opt-in, set allocator.coalescer.enabled=true in runtime config or via Console toggle. - To monitor impact: watch the new metrics allocator.coalescer.coalesce_success (should trend positive) and allocator.eviction_signal.count (should be low during steady state). - If p95 worsens after enabling, lower coalescer.cpu_budget_ms_per_scan or increase scan_interval_ms.

Related work: This addresses recurring production incidents where long lived fragmentation interacts badly with bursty large writes (see ENG-3245). Complements earlier softpin and reservation changes (previous PRs) by giving an async path to reduce fragmentation rather than only reactive pinning.

Notes on design alternatives considered: - Aggressive in-line compaction at allocation-time rejected due to latency impact. - Fully lockless global compaction was overly complex; hybrid opportunistic compaction using reclamation workers provides good tradeoff between complexity and effectiveness.

Summary: Low-risk background coalescer + eviction signalling reduces fragmentation and tail latency with tiny CPU cost and an opt-in switch for environments that need deterministic behaviour.
